Home · Services · Chemical Peeling

Treatment

Chemical Peeling

Chemical peels for selected concerns with skin tone and texture, with strength chosen for your skin.

About the treatment

A chemical peel applies a solution to the skin to remove surface layers in a controlled way. Different ingredients and depths are used for concerns such as uneven tone, acne marks or rough texture.

We choose the peel after checking your skin, current products and recent treatments. We also discuss recovery time so you can plan around work, sun exposure and events.

At a glance

  • May improve dullness and uneven tone
  • Options for some acne marks and pigmentation
  • May improve surface texture and fine lines
  • Advice on skincare before and after a peel
  • Peel depth chosen after assessment

The treatment process

  1. Consultation and assessment. We assess your skin, review your current products and check whether a peel is suitable now.
  2. A personal plan. We explain the treatment options, likely results, possible side effects and cost before you decide.
  3. The treatment itself. We talk you through the session and check how you feel as we go.
  4. Aftercare and follow up. We explain how to care for the treated area and when to contact us or return for a review.

Expected results

Skin may look more even and feel smoother once it has healed. The timing depends on peel depth, and some concerns need more than one session. We will review the result before recommending another peel.

Recovery & downtime

A superficial peel may cause mild redness or light flaking. A deeper peel can involve several days of visible peeling and needs more recovery time. Follow the aftercare plan, use the advised sun protection and avoid picking at peeling skin.

Who is it for?

Peels may be considered for uneven tone, some acne marks and rough texture. Active infection, irritation and certain medicines can affect timing or suitability, so a skin assessment comes first.

Frequently asked questions

Will my face visibly peel?
It depends on the peel and your skin. Even a superficial peel may cause some flaking, while deeper peels usually involve more visible shedding. We will explain what is likely with your treatment.
Do peels hurt?
Tingling, warmth or stinging can occur. We monitor your skin during the procedure. Tell us immediately if the sensation becomes painful so we can respond.
Can peels be done in summer?
Some superficial peels may be possible if you can follow sun protection and aftercare advice. Strong sun exposure can affect timing, especially for deeper peels. We will help you choose a suitable date.

plus prep and barrier care

as fresh skin surfaces

for tone and texture goals
